title: The Django scaffold
summary: The Django project behind ridwaanhall.com, set up before anything was public: one settings module, a core app, and the apps the site would grow into. 21 commits.

entries.body: Start the Django project with a core app and shared settings
Add the blog, career, dashboard, certificates and projects apps
Add the first page templates for the blog and home
Consolidate the settings into one module, with WhiteNoise for static files

title: The site goes live
summary: The first public version of the portfolio, deployed on Vercel: a home page, about, blog and projects with detail pages, a contact page, and a dashboard reading live GitHub and WakaTime activity. 260 commits.

entries.body: Add the about, contact, blog, projects and dashboard pages
List posts and render each one on its own page
Give every project a detail page at its own slug
Show GitHub contribution statistics on the dashboard
Add WakaTime coding activity beside them
Deploy on Vercel
Add the favicon, meta tags, a sitemap and robots.txt
Add a responsive header and mobile sidebar
Improve accessibility across the templates

title: Career, services and Django 5.2
summary: A month of filling the site in: the career page gained tabs, toggles and an interviews section, the home page gained services and featured posts, and the project moved to Django 5.2. 373 commits.

entries.body: Organise experience, education and certifications into tabs
Add an interviews section, with what each one taught
Expand and collapse responsibilities and achievements, animated
Add a services section and featured posts
Add a section supporting Palestine
Colour each post's tags
Add sponsorship links and issue templates
Upgrade to Django 5.2

title: Privacy policy, awards and the contribution graph
summary: The site gained a privacy policy, an awards tab, an interactive GitHub contributions graph and a stricter set of security headers, and every page moved to the Onest typeface. 201 commits.

entries.body: Publish a privacy policy page
Add an awards tab with credentials
Draw an interactive GitHub contributions graph
Add a content security policy and production-only security settings
Set the site in Onest
Show each school's location with a map link
Give every area its own Django app structure

title: Guestbook
summary: The biggest addition of the year: a guestbook where visitors sign in with Google and leave a message. The dashboard learned top languages, editors and systems from WakaTime, and the sidebar gained search. 396 commits.

entries.body: Add a guestbook with Google sign-in
Search the site from the sidebar, on mobile and desktop
Show top languages, categories and systems from WakaTime
Animate the progress bars and counters
Merge about and journey into one page with an introduction tab
Add GitHub and demo buttons, and a way back to the list
Add a sponsor section
Update Django to 5.2.2

title: Contact form and guestbook replies
summary: Visitors could now send a message from the contact page, and the guestbook grew up: replies, masked email addresses, Jakarta time and dismissible alerts. Images began to load through a resizing service. 203 commits.

entries.body: Send a message from the contact page
Show replies, including replies to yourself
Mask email addresses in messages
Show every timestamp in Jakarta time
Add alerts that dismiss themselves
Serve profile and logo images through a resizing service
Rewrite every page's title and description

title: Blog search and image optimisation
summary: The blog became searchable, every image on the site could be resized on the fly through wsrv.nl behind a feature flag, and the dashboard explained its streaks. 88 commits.

entries.body: Search the blog listing
Optimise images through wsrv.nl, behind a feature flag
Apply it to the blog and project templates
Explain the current and longest streak in a tooltip
Store dates as month and year, and show them that way
Update Django to 5.2.5

title: Open-hire
summary: A new open-hire page says whether I am open to work and what I am hiring for, linked from a status in the sidebar. 190 commits.

entries.body: Add the open-hire page: open to work, and hiring
Describe roles, skills, locations and how to get in touch
Link the hiring and open-to-work status to the page
Load skill icons through the image service
Fix the SEO configuration and meta tags

title: Image lightbox
summary: Project images open full size in a lightbox, and job applications show their salary range and a withdrawn status. 83 commits.

entries.body: Open project images in a lightbox
Show each application's salary range
Add a withdrawn status
Sort applications by their latest step
Smooth the skills carousel

title: Maintenance
summary: Dependency updates and a shorter dashboard cache, so the GitHub and WakaTime numbers stay fresher. 19 commits.

entries.body: Refresh the dashboard every 15 minutes instead of every 3 hours
Update Django

title: Maintenance
summary: Dependency updates, a fixed web manifest, and a credits section in the privacy policy. 13 commits.

entries.body: Serve the favicons in the web manifest from the site's own address
Add copyright and credits to the privacy policy
Update Django to 5.2.9

title: Email
summary: The contact form sends real email, protected by Cloudflare Turnstile, with an automatic reply to the sender, and new guestbook messages notify me by email. 53 commits.

entries.body: Deliver contact messages by email
Protect the form with Cloudflare Turnstile
Send the sender an automatic reply
Notify me of new guestbook messages
Open the full-resolution image
Describe the emails the site sends

title: Typed content
summary: Every post, project and profile record became a typed Python dataclass, and each app took ownership of its own data and tests. Guestbook notifications learned to tell a new message from a reply. 74 commits.

entries.body: Make every blog post, project and profile record a typed dataclass
Move each app's data into the app, with tests
Notify differently for a new message and a reply
Expand each role's details, animated
Record where each application was sent from

title: Security pass and a new mobile menu
summary: A security review closed a GraphQL injection, an exposed API key and two XSS paths, the mobile menu became a bottom sheet, and project pages gained a status badge. 73 commits.

entries.body: Fix a GraphQL injection, an API key exposure and an XSS
Send the API key in a header
Turn the mobile menu into a bottom sheet
Show each project's status and dates on its page
List the tools and skills I use
Correct the JSON-LD description and breadcrumb URL

title: A quieter home page
summary: The home page shows its sponsor, skills and blog sections only when there is something to show. 20 commits.

entries.body: Show the sponsor and blog sections only when they have content
Do the same for the skills section
Add uv to the skills

title: Maintenance
summary: Dependency updates and refreshed project images. 5 commits.

entries.body: Update dependencies
Refresh the MLBB identity card images

title: Maintenance
summary: A fixed test setup, refreshed experience, and dependency updates. 22 commits.

entries.body: Make pytest find and run the tests locally
Refresh the introduction and responsibilities

title: Status
summary: The sidebar can say when I am unwell, with an amber badge beside my name. 2 commits.

entries.body: Show an amber status badge when I am unwell

title: Pinned messages
summary: Guestbook messages can be pinned and links in them become clickable, with the races and XSS that came with it fixed before release. 20 commits.

entries.body: Pin messages, and detect links automatically
Fix an XSS and a race in pinning
Serialise concurrent pins

title: A database and an admin
summary: The content moved out of Python files and into a Supabase Postgres database, edited through the Django admin with structured editors instead of raw JSON. Everything readers see is cached and invalidated per area, and images are cleaned up once nothing uses them. 26 commits.

entries.body: Move the content from code into a Supabase database
Enable row-level security on every table
Edit lists and blocks with structured editors instead of JSON
Write posts with a structured content block editor
Delete stored images once nothing references them
Cache every read, invalidated per area
Merge guestbook history across databases

title: Comments
summary: Readers can comment on posts and projects, the privacy policy and terms became editable documents, and destructive actions ask first. 13 commits.

entries.body: Comment on blog posts and projects
Make the privacy policy and terms editable documents
Ask before destructive actions, site-wide
Redirect only to paths on this site after posting

title: Light and dark
summary: A light theme beside the dark one, animated, with every shadow removed; the guestbook became a threaded conversation; and tooltips started working on touch screens. 25 commits.

entries.body: Add a light/dark theme switch
Animate the switch and remove every shadow
Thread the guestbook and unify the site's notifications
Swipe the mobile drawer shut
Replace the click ripple with a spark
Make tooltips reachable on touch screens
Fix the structured data Search Console flagged

title: The last Django release
summary: Tailwind 4.3, one cache-busted stylesheet, and fonts served from the site itself. The final release of the Django site. 4 commits.

entries.body: Bundle every stylesheet into one cache-busted build
Serve fonts and icons from the site's own address
Upgrade to Tailwind 4.3

title: Rebuilt in Next.js
summary: The whole site rebuilt in Next.js on the same Supabase data, then the Django code removed. Every page was ported, the admin was rebuilt from scratch, sign-in moved to Auth.js, and the database was remodelled in its own schema keyed by UUID. 205 commits.

entries.body: Rebuild the site in Next.js and remove Django
Port the data layer to a typed API
Port every page: home, about, blog, projects, dashboard, open-hire, legal
Sign in with Auth.js
Port the threaded guestbook and comments
Build a new admin with forms, inlines and a rich-text editor
Upload images to Supabase Storage with reference counting
Remodel the data in its own schema, keyed by UUID
Keep row-level security on, and check it
